metadata.note: The Gettysburg and Harrisburg and its predecessors, Cumberland and Adams counties, Pennsylvania: the South Mountain Railroad (Carlisle - Mount Holly Springs - Hunter's Run - Pine Grove Furnace, completed 1870), the Gettysburg and Harrisburg Railroad (Hunter's Run - Gettysburg and the Round Top Branch, 1884), and the Gettysburg and Harrisburg Railway formed in 1891 under Philadelphia and Reading control, which ran it as the Reading's Gettysburg and Harrisburg branch until scheduled passenger service ended (1941; a 1947 date is unverified). Drawn per Rule 4 as South Mountain Railroad 1874-1891, G&H Railroad 1884-1891 (own track Hunter's Run - Gettysburg, and the Round Top Branch), Reading 1891-1941 (Carlisle - Gettysburg) and 1891-1939 (Round Top Branch), a single low-confidence 1904 anchor for the Hunter's Run and Slate Belt's Pine Grove Furnace line, and two later tourist operators on the same track: the Gettysburg Railroad (1995 [OPEN] - 1996) and Patriot Rail's Gettysburg Excursion Railway (2025 [OPEN]). Freight-only years are not drawn (Rule 1). Research report: research/branches/gettysburg_and_harrisburg_railway.txt.

metadata.ownership_split: Split at 1891 per the report's recommendation: the Philadelphia and Reading bought control of the G&H on 22 May 1891 and took 'formal possession at once', and the line was managed as a Reading branch thereafter, although the G&H Railway stayed a corporate subsidiary and no formal lease date was found. Reading-era features use the existing 'Philadelphia and Reading Railroad / Reading Company' company string and colour (pulled from reading_main_line.geojson); the label names the Philadelphia and Reading, which ran it for 33 of the 50 drawn years (Reading Company from 1924).

segments.note: South Mountain Railroad (1870-1877), then South Mountain Railway and Mining Co. (1877-1891): iron-company line from the Cumberland Valley at Gettysburg (South Mountain) Junction east of Carlisle via Bonny Brook, Craighead's, Mount Holly Springs, Upper Mill and Hunter's Run to Henry Clay, Laurel and Pine Grove Furnace. Steam throughout. START 1874 is the first CONFIRMED year of scheduled passenger service (2 Jun 1874: '8 scheduled stops between its terminus and South Mountain Junction'; a Dec 1875 report lists 9 passenger stations; Fowler's 1875 Official Guide letter 'y' on the stations). The line was completed in 1870, but 1870-1873 passenger service is unproven and not drawn. END 1891 is a change of operator, not a service end: the northern section (Carlisle - Hunter's Run) merged into the Gettysburg and Harrisburg Railway on 20 Jul 1891 (Reading-controlled - see the Philadelphia and Reading feature) and the Hunter's Run - Pine Grove Furnace section was leased to the Hunter's Run and Slate Belt on 13 Jul 1891. From 1884 the Gettysburg and Harrisburg Railroad's trains also ran over this track between Hunter's Run and Carlisle and to Pine Grove Park for excursions; they are not drawn twice (the G&H feature draws only its own Hunter's Run - Gettysburg track). Who physically worked Carlisle - Hunter's Run trains 1884-1891 (SMRR or G&H) is not established. Headway 360 min is an ESTIMATE from the Cumberland Valley's 1884 advertisement of three connecting trains a day each way 'For Mt. Holly, Pinegrove Furnace and Gettysburg'; no SMRR timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: start from the 2 Jun 1874 schedule and Dec 1875 station report as cited by Wikipedia's South Mountain Railroad article, and Fowler's 1875 Official Guide letter 'y' (sec. 177); end from the 1891 merger and lease (Wikipedia); headway estimated from the 31 May 1884 CV advertisement. As read in research/branches/gettysburg_and_harrisburg_railway.txt block [1].

segments.note: Gettysburg and Harrisburg Railroad (chartered 6 Oct 1882; supt. W. H. Woodward), built by Jay Cooke / Jackson C. Fuller interests to reach the battlefield from the north: Hunter's Run - Goodyear - Starner's - Peach Glen - Idaville - Gardners - Bendersville - Biglerville - Table Rock - Goldenville - Gettysburg. START 1884 exact: first train 26 Feb 1884, scheduled passenger service from 21 Apr 1884. Through trains ran on from Hunter's Run to Carlisle (Cumberland Valley connection) over South Mountain Railroad track; that track is drawn for these years by the South Mountain Railroad feature and is deliberately not drawn twice here. END 1891 is a change of control, not a service end: the Philadelphia and Reading took control on 22 May 1891 and the Gettysburg and Harrisburg Railway was formed 20 Jul 1891; service continues on the Philadelphia and Reading feature. Headway 360 min is an ESTIMATE from the 1884 Cumberland Valley advertisement of three connecting trains a day each way; no G&H timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: start from Wikipedia's Gettysburg and Harrisburg Railroad article (citing the Gettysburg Compiler 1883-85, NYT 27 Feb 1884, Star & Sentinel 4 Mar 1884); end from the Reading's purchase of control (Evening Herald, Shenandoah, 25 May 1891 p.1); headway estimated from the 31 May 1884 CV advertisement. As read in research/branches/gettysburg_and_harrisburg_railway.txt block [2].

segments.note: Round Top Branch, built May-June 1884 from the G&H north of the Meade School via Hancock station (south of the Angle) and the Fairfield Road siding to the G&H's Little Round Top Park, to carry battlefield visitors. Excursion and special trains only, never a scheduled line - hence tourist_rail; service was seasonal and occasion-driven, so a continuous span overstates frequency, though not the years in which excursions ran. Steam 'dummy' and locomotives; no animal power. START 1884 exact: track laid May 1884, Round Top station warehouse finished 21 Jun 1884, steam-dummy excursions from June 1884. END 1891: the Philadelphia and Reading took control of the G&H on 22 May 1891 - a change of operator, not a service end (continued on the Philadelphia and Reading Round Top Branch feature, identical geometry). Headway 1440 min is a placeholder for occasional excursion service, not a counted frequency.

segments.note: The Reading's battlefield route, Carlisle (Gettysburg Junction) - Bonny Brook - Craighead's - Carlisle Junction - Mount Holly Springs - Hunter's Run - Bendersville - Biglerville - Gettysburg, run as the Gettysburg and Harrisburg Railway under Philadelphia and Reading control from 22 May 1891 ('formal possession at once'; McLeod president) and the Reading Company from 1924: local Harrisburg - Gettysburg trains (via the Reading's own line to Carlisle Junction) plus excursions from Philadelphia and Reading. Contemporary references to it as a Reading line: 1895 court case (the G&H Railway 'which is controlled by the Reading', 'its schedule of trains'); 1915 'Bonnybrook station on the Gettysburg and Harrisburg branch of the Reading railroad ... killed by a passenger train'; 1918 'the Gettysburg and Harrisburg division' among the Reading's branches west of the Susquehanna. No formal lease date was found; a final merger into the Reading Company (1945?) is unverified. END 1941 - SOURCE CONFLICT: Wikipedia (G&H Railway, Round Top Branch and Gettysburg station articles, citing the Gettysburg Times) says Reading passenger service to Gettysburg ended in 1941 'except for special occasions'; Trains.com (Jan 2024, page unreadable - known only from a search summary, UNVERIFIED) says scheduled passenger service from Harrisburg ended behind camelback 4-6-0 No. 615 on 27 Apr 1947. Drawn to the earlier, 1941. A possible reconciliation - service to Gettysburg ending 1941 with a cut-back Harrisburg - Carlisle Jct / Mount Holly train to 1947 - is NOT established; if it is ever proven it would extend only the Carlisle Jct - Mount Holly Springs piece. The Feb 1952 Official Guide (Oct 1951 schedules) prints 'Freight Service' against the G&H stations, so the branch was certainly freight-only by 1951. Freight continued under the Reading to 1976 and later owners; Carlisle - Mount Holly Springs was lifted c.1955 (not drawn - Rule 1). Reading excursions of 1958 and 1960-64 are unverified and not drawn. Headway 360 min is an ESTIMATE; no Reading timetable for the branch was read.
sources: Segment-level: start from the Reading's purchase of control (Evening Herald, Shenandoah, 25 May 1891 p.1); Reading-era service from the Evening Herald 27 Jun 1895 p.4 and Harrisburg Telegraph 24 Aug 1915 p.1 and 18 Jul 1918 p.14; end 1941 from Wikipedia citing the Gettysburg Times, CONFLICTING with an unverified Trains.com 1947 date; freight-only by Oct 1951 from the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 16. Headway estimated. As read in research/branches/gettysburg_and_harrisburg_railway.txt block [4].

segments.note: [ANCHOR] - LOW CONFIDENCE. The Hunter's Run and Slate Belt Railroad (Fuller Brick & Slate interests, not the Reading) leased the South Mountain's Hunter's Run - Toland - Henry Clay - Laurel - Pine Grove Park - Pine Grove Furnace section from 13 Jul 1891 until the G&H Railway / Reading took it back on 31 Oct 1910 (or 11 Nov 1910 - the Wikipedia articles disagree). THE ENTIRE EVIDENCE for passenger service in its years is (a) a Feb 1904 roster of 2 locomotives and 3 passenger cars and (b) a general statement that the line 'served Pine Grove Park for excursions'. No dated passenger train has been found. 1904 is drawn as the one year tied to passenger equipment; service certainly ran wider both ways if it ran at all, but no other year is confirmed - do not widen this anchor without evidence, and do not delete it to tidy the map. Whether excursions to Pine Grove Park were HR&SB trains or G&H/Reading trains running through over the lease is not established. The 5.12 mi Slate Belt extension beyond Pine Grove Furnace (1892) has no passenger evidence and is not drawn; passenger service after 1910 under the Reading is unknown and not drawn. Headway 1440 min is a placeholder, not a counted frequency.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia's Hunter's Run and Slate Belt Railroad article (Feb 1904 roster with 3 passenger cars; 'served Pine Grove Park for excursions'); lease dates from the same and the South Mountain Railroad article. No dated passenger train is sourced. As read in research/branches/gettysburg_and_harrisburg_railway.txt block [5].

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 24.3 mi Gettysburg - Mount Holly Springs against a documented 23.4 mi (Wikipedia, Gettysburg Railroad line) / 25 mi (Gettysburg & Northern today), 104% / 97%. Same geometry as the G&H Hunter's Run - Gettysburg trace plus the active Gettysburg and Northern Mount Holly Springs - Hunter's Run (traced, no straight-line leg): 23.6 mi on Gettysburg and Northern track, 0.7 mi on untagged OSM track into the old G&H depot. The Mount Holly Springs end is the G&N track at 40.1174 N 77.1825 W; the Gettysburg end is the Gettysburg & Harrisburg depot site - where the 1990s excursions actually boarded in Gettysburg is not established. Drawn on the present-day track, which is the alignment these excursions used.

segments.note: Gettysburg Railroad (1976-1996; Blairsville & Indiana interests), tourist arm Gettysburg Passenger Services: steam and later diesel excursions over the former G&H between Gettysburg and Mount Holly Springs. A different company from the G&H, on its track. START 1995 is [OPEN] - it is the first year tied to a dated excursion operation (No. 1278's boiler explosion near Gardners, 16 Jun 1995; diesel only afterwards), NOT the year excursions began: american-rails.com says excursions ran 'by the late 1970s' and the company had four steam locomotives (two by 1988), but no earlier dated trip has been found. Do not move the start earlier without a dated trip. END 1996: the company 'ceased its excursions and freight services in late 1996' and was sold in Nov 1996. The excursions' exact route length (to Mount Holly Springs, or shorter) is not established. Headway 10080 min (weekly) is a placeholder for seasonal excursions, not a counted frequency.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia's Gettysburg Railroad (1976-1996) article (16 Jun 1995 boiler explosion; excursions ceased late 1996) and american-rails.com. Start is the earliest confirmed year only. As read in research/branches/gettysburg_and_harrisburg_railway.txt block [6].

segments.note: Gettysburg Excursion Railway, run by Patriot Rail (owner of the Gettysburg & Northern since 2022) over the former G&H: round trips Gettysburg - Biglerville per local reporting (the line runs on to Mount Holly Springs; an extension of the excursions is 'planned' only). START 2025: Patriot Rail's press release of 7 Aug 2025 says it was 'set to open to the public later this month'; Wikipedia says service 'began in mid-2025'. END 2025 is [OPEN]: the Gettysburgian of 14 Dec 2025 describes it operating, and 2025 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - the railway is believed still running, but no 2026 source has been checked. Do not extend without a 2026 source. Headway 10080 min (weekly) is a placeholder for scheduled excursions, not a counted frequency.
